newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Unemployed mother leads thousands in Swedish march.
newsitem.headline: Unemployed mother leads thousands in Swedish march.

text.p: An unemployed Swedish mother-of-four led an estimated 6,000 demonstrators through the streets of Stockholm on Tuesday to protest against plans to trim workers' rights.
Therese Rajaniemi, 31, urged trade unions to consider calling a general strike on December 12, the day when parliament debates proposed changes to labour protection law.
Employers say the changes are needed to create more flexibility in the labour market.
But trade unions, which supported but did not organise Tuesday's march, complain that the changes would erode Sweden's once-hallowed job security.

The marchers, who came to Stockholm from all parts of Sweden, also warned the Social Democratic government of Prime Minister Goran Persson not to try to introduce cost-cutting changes to the unemployment benefit system.
Rajaniemi, who organised a similar demonstration outside parliament on October 17, met Persson for two hours on Monday evening and said she would meet him again before December 12.

Swedish unemployment is officially listed as 7.8 percent, already high by Swedish standards, but the figure rises to 13 percent when the number of people out of work and on training courses is included.
The Swedish manufacturing industries organisation said on Tuesday that production was now at the bottom of the cycle but would pick up next year, possibly leading to some new jobs in 1998.
